ThingDef.label: AK Lyutiy-Kannel
ThingDef.description:
Caliber: 7.62x39mm. 30-round detachable mag. Select-Fire.
The AK (Avtomat Kalashnikova) is a Soviet assault rifle designed between 1946-1947 by Mikhail Kalashnikov. Commonly (and somewhat anachronistically) known as the "AK-47," the AK is one of the most recognizable and widely used weapons platforms ever made, with over 100 million Kalashnikov-type guns having been produced since 1948. Reputed for its ease of mass production and reliability, the AK was the backbone of the Soviet Armed Forces and continues to be the standard service platform in most former Warsaw Pact nations.
The early line of AK rifles consists of three major variants - the Type I (produced from 1948/49 to 1951), Type II (1951-1954/55), and Type III (1955-1959.) Type I AKs had stamped sheet metal receivers, while the subsequent Type II had a milled receiver. The Type III was a further update that lightened the milled receiver.
This rifle is a special prototype Type I with modifications designed by Soviet officers and engineers Vasiliy Luyity and Boris Kannel. Made from some of the very first serial production AK rifles, the Lyutiy-Kannel AK was designed to fix some of the major perceived flaws in the production design. Changes to the base included a pistol grip at a less sharp angle, a longer handguard, a slightly lengthier stock, a thicker barrel profile, and a mid-bore brake "stabilizer." All of these changes were aimed to improve the accuracy of the weapon, which had exceptional issues when fired fully-automatic or in bursts. Their proposed changes were not accepted and the Type I AK was produced in its original configuration, but the reduced grip angle would later be introduced for the Type II, and the handguard was modified on the later AKM.
